rounding.notes: Applied at publication only; all intermediate arithmetic is full-precision decimal. dated_siu rounds to significant figures, not a fixed decimal-place count, so its precision scales with the price rather than being lost as it falls (found live, 2026-09-25 — see docs/methodology.md's Rounding section). basket_cost carries more decimal places than dated_siu needs at any price level so the published print stays reproducible from its own published figures. siu_per_usd truncates so it never overstates the work a dollar buys.

correction_notes.note: This print is correctly computed under the current methodology and passed every gate at cut-off; it is not being revised. The drop from 2026-09-25's $0.0111 to $0.007626 reflects a change in which constituents had real run records today, not market movement: gemini-3.1-pro-preview — the single most expensive constituent yesterday at $0.039236/basket — produced zero run records today because of a real Google API billing outage ("prepayment credits depleted"), while claude-haiku-4-5, excluded yesterday for the same reason (zero run records), returned with real, qualifying runs. The site's "registry changed" marker correctly did not fire for today's print: both models remain registered constituents throughout; only their per-print qualifying status changed, which computeConstituentChanges is deliberately scoped to ignore (see methodology.md's registry inclusion policy) so a bad day is never confused with an actual registry removal. That said, this print's own event exposes a real, known methodology gap: the pipeline currently treats a constituent with no run records on a given day as simply absent from the equal-weighted mean, with no link ratio bridging the day it drops out and the day it returns — a provider outage is currently indistinguishable, in the computed number, from an unannounced rebalance. A fix (separating per-print availability from registry membership, with capped carry-forward imputation and a chain-linked rebalance) is planned, not yet implemented. For reference only, and never a replacement for the signed value above: recomputing today's equal-weighted mean with gemini-3.1-pro-preview's last valid measured cost ($0.039236, from 2026-09-25) carried forward in place of its missing measurement gives $0.010787 — closer to the trend this print's own drop otherwise misrepresents as a market move.

Correction to this print's own correction note above: that note described gemini-3.1-pro-preview's zero run records as caused by "a real Google API billing outage." That mischaracterises whose failure this was. The actual cause was this project's own Google Cloud billing account lapsing — prepayment credits on our account were depleted — not any outage, degradation, or failure on Google's side. Google's API was reachable and functioning normally throughout; the requests never had valid billing behind them because of a lapse on our side. Same underlying fact the original note already quoted correctly ("prepayment credits depleted") — only the surrounding framing was wrong, and is corrected here. Separately: the methodology gap this print's own note called "planned, not yet implemented" has since been implemented — a model missing today's run records now carries its last real, published cost forward for up to 3 calendar days before being excluded, and every print now also publishes an unweighted median as a diagnostic alongside the mean. See docs/methodology.md's Aggregation section (rules-2026-09-26) for the full retro-validated evidence, including this print's own $0.010787 carry-forward figure, computed identically by the shipped implementation.
